# 1 Maccabees Chapter 9 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_009_page_001.jpg

---

**1** When Demetrius heard that Nicanor had fallen along with his forces in battle, he sent Bacchides and Alcimus into the land of Judah a second time, together with the right wing of his army.

**2** They marched along the road that leads to Gilgal and encamped against Mesaloth in Arbela; they captured it and killed many people.

**3** In the first month of the one hundred and fifty-second year they encamped against Jerusalem.

**4** Then they set out and marched to Berea with twenty thousand infantry and two thousand cavalry.

**5** Judas was encamped at Elasa with three thousand picked men.

**6** But when they saw the great size of the enemy force, they were badly frightened, and many deserted the camp until only eight hundred remained.

**7** When Judas saw that his army had melted away and that the battle was pressing upon him, he was crushed in spirit, for he had no time to gather them.

**8** Yet he gathered his strength and said to those who remained: "Let us rise and go up against our enemies; perhaps we can still fight them."

**9** But they tried to turn him back, saying: "We cannot. Let us save our lives now and come back with our brothers to fight them; but we are too few."

**10** Judas replied: "Far be it from me to do such a thing as to flee from them. If our hour has come, let us die bravely for our brothers, and leave no cause for reproach against our honor."

**11** Then the enemy army marched out of the camp and took its position to meet them. The cavalry was divided into two companies, and the slingers and the archers went before the army, and all the most powerful warriors were in front.

**12** Bacchides was stationed on the right wing, while the phalanx advanced from both sides to the sound of the trumpets.

**13** The men of Judas also blew the trumpets, and the earth shook from the noise of the two armies, and the battle raged from morning until evening.

**14** Judas saw that Bacchides and the strength of his army were positioned on the right, and all the courageous men rallied around him.

**15** The right wing was broken, and he pursued them as far as Mount Azotus.

**16** Those on the left wing, seeing that the right had been broken, turned and followed in the footsteps of Judas and of those with him from the rear.

**17** The battle became fierce, and many on both sides fell wounded.

**18** Then Judas fell, and the rest fled.

**19** Jonathan and Simon carried off their brother Judas and buried him in the tomb of his ancestors at Modein.

**20** They wept for him, and all Israel made great lamentation and mourned for him for many days, saying:

**21** "How has the mighty fallen, the savior of Israel!"

**22** As for the remaining acts of Judas — his wars, his brave deeds, and his greatness — they have not been recorded, for they were very many.

**23** After the death of Judas, the lawless men raised their heads in all the territory of Israel, and all the workers of iniquity broke out again.

**24** In those days a very severe famine occurred, and the country went over to their side.

**25** Bacchides deliberately chose renegade men and appointed them lords of the country.

**26** They sought out and hunted down the friends of Judas and brought them to Bacchides, who took vengeance on them and abused them.

**27** It was a great tribulation in Israel, the like of which had not been since the time prophets ceased to appear to them.

**28** Then all the friends of Judas assembled and said to Jonathan:

**29** "Since your brother Judas died, there has been no one like him to go against our enemies and against Bacchides and against those who hate our nation.

**30** So now we have chosen you today to be our leader and commander in his place, to fight our battles."

**31** Jonathan accepted the leadership at that time and took the place of his brother Judas.

**32** When Bacchides learned of this, he sought to kill him.

**33** Jonathan and his brother Simon and all those with him, when they learned of this, fled into the wilderness of Tekoa and encamped beside the pool of Asphar.

**34** Bacchides learned of this on the Sabbath, and he came with all his forces across the Jordan.

**35** Jonathan sent his brother as leader of the people to ask the Nabateans his friends to deposit with them their large amount of baggage.

**36** But the sons of Jambri came out from Medaba and seized John and everything he had, and departed with it.

**37** After these things, Jonathan and Simon his brother were told that the sons of Jambri were celebrating a great wedding and were escorting the bride from Nadabath — the daughter of one of the great nobles of Canaan — with a large retinue.

**38** They remembered the blood of John their brother and went up and hid themselves under cover of the mountainside.

**39** They looked and saw a noisy crowd with much baggage; then the bridegroom came out along with his friends and brothers to meet them with tambourines and musicians and many weapons.

**40** The men of Judas rose up from their ambush against them and struck them down; many fell slain, and the survivors fled to the mountain, while the Jews took all their spoils.

**41** So the wedding was turned to mourning and the sound of their music into lamentation.

**42** Having thus avenged the blood of their brother, they returned to the marshes of the Jordan.

**43** When Bacchides heard of this, he came on the Sabbath day to the banks of the Jordan with a large force.

**44** Jonathan said to those with him: "Let us get up now and fight for our lives; the situation today is not the same as before.

**45** For see, the battle is in front of us and behind us, and the waters of the Jordan on this side and on that, and there is marsh and thicket, and there is no place to turn.

**46** Now therefore cry out to Heaven that you may be delivered from the hand of your enemies."

**47** The battle was joined; Jonathan stretched out his hand to strike Bacchides, but Bacchides drew back from him.

**48** Jonathan and those with him jumped into the Jordan and swam across to the other side, and the enemy did not cross the Jordan to pursue them.

**49** About one thousand from Bacchides' side fell that day.

**50** Then Bacchides returned to Jerusalem and built strongly fortified cities in Judea: the fortress at Jericho, at Emmaus, at Beth-horon, at Bethel, at Timnath, at Pharathon, and at Tephon — with high walls and gates and bars.

**51** He stationed garrisons in them to harass Israel.

**52** He also fortified Beth-zur and Gazara and the citadel, and he put troops and provisions in them.

**53** He took the sons of the leading men of the land as hostages and put them under guard in the citadel in Jerusalem.

**54** In the one hundred and fifty-third year, in the second month, Alcimus gave orders to tear down the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary, thus destroying the work of the prophets. And he had begun to tear it down

**55** when, at that very moment, Alcimus was struck down; his work was hindered, and his mouth was stopped. He was paralyzed and could no longer say a word or give instructions about his house.

**56** Alcimus died at that time in great agony.

**57** When Bacchides saw that Alcimus was dead, he returned to the king, and the land of Judah was at rest for two years.

**58** Then all the lawless men consulted together, saying: "Jonathan and his men are living in security and confidence. Now therefore let us bring Bacchides here, and he will seize them all in a single night."

**59** So they went and consulted with him.

**60** He started to come with a large force and secretly sent letters to all his allies who were in Judea, telling them to seize Jonathan and those with him. But they were unable to do it, because the plot became known.

**61** The men of Jonathan and his companions seized about fifty of those ringleaders of the conspiracy who were in the land and killed them.

**62** Then Jonathan and Simon and their companions withdrew to Bethbasi in the wilderness; they rebuilt its ruins and strengthened it.

**63** When Bacchides learned of this, he assembled his whole force and sent word to those in Judea.

**64** He came and besieged Bethbasi, and he fought against it for many days and made siege engines.

**65** Jonathan slipped away and left Simon his brother in the city, while he himself went out into the countryside with a select force.

**66** He struck down Odomera and his brothers and the sons of Phaseron in their tents; then they began to strike and advance into battle.

**67** Simon and his men sallied out from the city and burned the siege engines.

**68** They fought against Bacchides and he was crushed by them; they distressed him severely, for his campaign and his plan had come to nothing.

**69** He was greatly angered against the lawless men who had counseled him to come into the land, and he killed many of them; then he decided to go back to his own land.

**70** When Jonathan learned of this, he sent ambassadors to him to make peace with him and to secure the release of prisoners.

**71** Bacchides accepted this gladly and acted on his proposals, swearing to Jonathan that he would do him no harm for the rest of his life.

**72** He handed over the prisoners he had previously taken in the land of Judea, and returned and went back to his own land, never to enter their territory again.

**73** Thus the sword ceased from Israel, and Jonathan settled at Michmash. There he began to judge the people, and he exterminated the godless from Israel.
